'''Muhammad Hafeez Qureshi''' ([[Urdu]]: محمد حفيظ قريشى) (31 October 1930 – 11 August 2007), {{small|[[Nishan-e-Imtiaz|NI]], [[Sitara-e-Imtiaz|SI]], [[Hilal-i-Imtiaz|HI]]}}, known as '''Hafeez Qureshi''', was a Pakistani [[nuclear scientist]] and a [[mechanical engineer]], known for his role as a diagnostics engineer for his nation's [[nuclear capability]].<ref name=Lancer>{{cite book|last1=Verma|first1=Anand K.|title=Reassessing Pakistan : role of two nation theory|date=2001|publisher=Lancer|location=New Delhi|isbn=978-8170622871|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=zJEp2I5BIIAC&pg=PA249}}</ref>

His career was spent working at the [[Pakistan Institute of Nuclear Science & Technology]] as overseeing the diagnostics on the [[Subcritical reactor|subcritical experiments]] on the [[nuclear weapon]]s where he gained expertise in engineering applications of [[nuclear physics]].<ref name="Pakistan link" />

==Biography==

===Early life and education===
Muhammad Hafeez Qureshi was born in [[Kapurthala]], in [[Punjab]], [[British India]], to a [[Punjabi language|Punjabi-speaking]] [[Indian Muslim|Muslim family]] on 31 October 1930.{{rp|1256}}<ref name="Vallancey Press, 1969">{{cite book |title=Who's who in Atoms |date=1969 |publisher=Vallancey Press |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=pNfaAAAAMAAJ&q=HAFEEZ+ |language=en}}</ref> His family [[Indians in Pakistan|emigrated]] from [[India]] to [[Pakistan]] sometime after the [[partition of India]] in 1947; they settled in [[Karachi]], [[Sindh]].<ref name="Pakistan link"/> Upon matriculating from a local high school, Qureshi enrolled at [[Karachi University]] in 1956; he partly supported his studies by working as a [[motor mechanic]].<ref name="Pakistan link">{{Cite web|url=http://pakistanlink.org/Opinion/2007/Aug07/24/08.HTM|title=An Unsung Hero Passes away|last=Jameel|first=Dr. Muhammad|author2=Akhtar M. Faruqui|date=24 August 2007|website=Pakistan Link|access-date=14 June 2019|archive-date=2 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211102053905/https://www.pakistanlink.org//Opinion/2007/Aug07/24/08.HTM|url-status=live}}</ref>

In his dormitory at the university, his schoolmate and friend was notable future [[optical physicist]] Dr. Muhammad Jameel— who was also present when Pakistan tested its nuclear devices in [[Ras Koh Range]].<ref name="Pakistan link"/> He attained a [[Bachelor of Science]] (BSc) in [[physics]] and earned a scholarship to resume his studies at [[Michigan State University]] (MSU) in the [[United States]].{{rp|179–190}}<ref name="Stanford University Press">{{cite book|last1=Khan|first1=Feroz Hassan|title=Eating grass the making of the Pakistani bomb|date=2012|publisher=Stanford University Press|location=Palo Alto|isbn=978-0804784801|pages=179–190 of 521|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=yGgrNAsKZjEC&pg=PA179|format=google books}}</ref>

At MSU, Qureshi enrolled in the engineering department and gained a [[Bachelor of Science]] (BS) in mechanical engineering, followed by a [[Master of Science]] (MS), also in mechanical engineering<ref name="Stanford University Press"/> His mechanical engineering thesis contained work on applications of the [[mechanics of materials]].<ref name="Stanford University Press"/> In 1960, he was admitted into the [[Doctorate|doctoral program]] in mechanical engineering at MSU, but left his [[Doctor of Philosophy|doctoral studies]] for unknown reasons.{{rp|1256}}<ref name="Vallancey Press, 1969" />

After returning to Pakistan in 1960, Qureshi joined Karachi Mechanical Laboratories (KML) and found employment with the [[Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission]] (PAEC) in 1963, where he joined the staff led by Dr. [[Naeem Ahmad Khan]] in Lahore.<ref name="The Nation, SBM, 2007">{{cite news |last1=Mahmood |first1=S. B. |author1-link=Sultan Bashiruddin Mahmood |title=Obituary: Hafeez Qureshi, a great scientist passes away |work=The writer is former Director General (Nuclear Power) of Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission. |agency=The Nation |publisher=The Nation, Mahmood, 2007 |date=15 August 2007 |location=Islamabad |language=en-pk}}</ref>

==Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission==

In 1963, Qureshi served as design engineer at the Atomic Energy Center in Lahore where he oversaw the installation of the first [[neutron generator]].<ref name="Pakistan link" /> In 1965, Qureshi moved to [[Nilore]] to join [[Pakistan Institute of Nuclear Science and Technology]] (PINSTECH) where he was part of the team that designed his nation's first nation's [[nuclear pile]] —[[Pakistan Atomic Research Reactor#PARR-I Reactor|PARR-I]] reactor at Pinstech Laboratory in Nilore which went [[Subcritical reactor|critical]] in 1965.<ref>{{harvnb|Rahman|1998|pp=11}}</ref><ref>{{harvnb|Rahman|1998|pp=10–11}}</ref> In 1967, Qureshi moved to the Nuclear Physics Group working under [[Naeem Ahmad Khan]] that was investigating on the feasibility of the [[gas centrifuge]]s for the industrial enrichment.<ref name="The Nation, 2007">{{cite news|last1=Mahmood|first1=Sultan Bashiruddin|title=Hafeez Qureshi: A great scientist passes away|url=http://nation.com.pk/.|access-date=10 November 2014|agency=The Nation|publisher=The Nation, 2007|date=15 August 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141111013721/http://nation.com.pk/|archive-date=11 November 2014|url-status=bot: unknown}}</ref>

This study group also included [[Sultan Bashiruddin Mahmood|Sultan Mahmood]] and [[Samar Mubarakmand]] but left the project when he joined the Radiation Isotope Application Division (RIAD) at the laboratory under Naeem Ahmad Khan.<ref>{{harvnb|Rahman|1998|pp=70–71}}</ref> In December 1971, Qureshi was made director of RIAD with support provided from Dr. Naeem Ahmad.<ref name="Defence Journal">{{Cite web|url=http://www.defencejournal.com/2000/june/chagai.htm|title=When Mountains Move – The Story of Chagai: §The Wah Group: Designers and Manufacturers of Pakistan's Nuclear Device|last=Azam|first=Rai Muhammad Saleh|date=June 2000|website=Defence Journal|publisher=The Nation|access-date=14 June 2019|archive-date=1 April 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120401181303/http://www.defencejournal.com/2000/june/chagai.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===1971 war and atomic bomb project===

In 1974, Qureshi was invited by [[Munir Ahmad Khan]] and [[Abdus Salam]] to participate in the development of nuclear weapons when he was asked to design, engineer, and machine the [[mechanical design|design components]], [[Tamper (nuclear weapon)|tampers]], and [[explosive lens]]es necessary for detonation of the [[nuclear weapon]].{{rp|179–180}}<ref name="Stanford University Press, Khan, 2012">{{cite book |last1=Khan |first1=Feroz |title=Eating Grass: The Making of the Pakistani Bomb |date=7 November 2012 |publisher=Stanford University Press |isbn=978-0-8047-8480-1 |pages=500 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=yGgrNAsKZjEC |access-date=30 March 2024 |language=en}}</ref> He soon joined the Metallurgical Laboratory (ML) located in [[Wah Cantonment]] and collaborated with Dr. Zaman Sheikh, a physical chemist and authority on [[Explosives engineering|explosives]], of [[Defence Science & Technology Organization]] (DESTO).{{rp|189–190}}<ref name="Georgetown University Press, Ahmed, 2022">{{cite book |last1=Ahmed |first1=Mansoor |title=Pakistan's Pathway to the Bomb: Ambitions, Politics, and Rivalries |date=1 May 2022 |publisher=Georgetown University Press |location=Washington DC, U.S. |isbn=978-1-64712-232-4 |pages=291 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ACdZEAAAQBAJ&dq=hafeez+qureshi&pg=PA189 |access-date=30 March 2024 |language=en}}</ref> This led to the establishment of the Wah Group Scientist (WGS) at the ML that worked on metallurgical aspect of the nuclear device.<ref name="Defence Journal"/><ref>{{harvnb|Rahman|1998|pp=38}}</ref><ref>{{harvnb|Rahman|1998|pp=70–85}}</ref> Several sessions were held on the feasibility of the device between the Wah Group Scientist with the Abdus Salam and Riazuddin of Theoretical Physics Group (TPG); [[Asghar Qadir]] and [[Munir Ahmad Rashid]] of the Mathematical Physics Group; [[Ishfaq Ahmad]] of Nuclear Physics Division.<ref>{{harvnb|Rahman|1998|pp=38–39}}</ref> During the meeting, the word [[Atomic bomb|''bomb'']] was never used, instead the scientists used scientific research rationale.<ref>{{harvnb|Rahman|1998|pp=39}}</ref> There, the scientists decided to develop an 'implosion' over the 'gun' type fission device citing economy in the use of [[fissile material]].<ref>{{harvnb|Rahman|1998|pp=39–40}}</ref>

The Wah Group Scientists also took initiatives in designing of high precision mechanical and chemical components – how tampers would be developed to produce efficiency and high precision data – physics calculations – what would its appropriate time reaction be when the explosives make contact with the material– high explosives– what kind of chemistry be would be used, and triggering mechanisms – how the weapon would be detonated.<ref>{{harvnb|Rahman|1998|pp=76–78}}</ref> Since the testing facilities in [[Pakistan Institute of Nuclear Science & Technology|PINSTECH]] Nilore lacked, the ML performed several explosives experiments and chemistry measurements in cooperation with the [[Pakistan Ordnance Factories]] (POF), which was the source of providing the explosives, in 1976.<ref>{{harvnb|Rahman|1998|pp=55–60}}</ref>

By 1979, the Wah Group Scientists under Hafeez and Sheikh had developed the wide range of explosive lenses, design components finished on the [[computer numerical control]], the polymer-based high explosive materials, and triggering mechanisms.{{rp|180}}<ref name="Georgetown University Press, Ahmed, 2022"/><ref>{{harvnb|Rahman|1998|pp=85–88}}</ref><ref>{{harvnb|Rahman|1998|pp=80}}</ref>

===Subcritical testing and diagnostics===
In 1980, the Wah Group Scientist team collaborated with the Diagnostics Directorate in designing the diagnostics to viability and reliability of the first nuclear device without the use of nuclear testing.{{rp|194}}<ref name="Georgetown University Press, Ahmed, 2022" /> The [[Prompt criticality|subcritical]] experiments on the physical package was organized in the secret [[Kirana Hills Site]], controlled by the [[Pakistan Air Force]], under the test series: [[Kirana-I]].<ref>{{harvnb|Rahman|1998|pp=89–90}}</ref> The first subcritical experiment on the first nuclear device took place on 11 March 1983.<ref>{{harvnb|Rahman|1998|pp=91}}</ref> The diagnostics and the subcritical experiments continued on 24 different improved designs, developed by TPG, under [[Samar Mubarakmand]] of the Diagnostics Directorate and Hafeez Qureshi of Wah Group Scientist.<ref>{{harvnb|Rahman|1998|pp=92–93}}</ref>{{rp|184–190}}<ref name="Stanford University Press, Khan, 2012" />

Hafeez Qureshi, alongside Samar Mubarakmand, oversaw the diagnostics and subcritical testing program of nuclear weapons as its test director until the full-scale nuclear testing ([[Chagai-I]]) was conducted at the [[Ras Koh Range]] in 1998.<ref>{{harvnb|Rahman|1998|pp=105}}</ref>

==Death and honors==

On 11 August 2007, Qureshi died from natural causes, aged 76.<ref name="Pakistan link" /><ref name="The Nation, SBM, 2007" /> After his retirement, he served on the mechanical engineering faculty at the [[Pakistan Institute of Engineering and Applied Sciences]], and was honored with his nation's highest honors including the [[Sitara-e-Imtiaz]] in 1992 and [[Hilal-e-Imtiaz]] in 2002 conferred by the [[President of Pakistan]].<ref name="The Nation, SBM, 2007" />

In 2023, the Government of Pakistan accepted the recommendation to honor his services with the [[Nishan-i-Imtiaz]], which he was awarded in 2024.<ref name="Dawn Newspapers, APP, 2024" />
